reference.jd_text:
# Posting Record: AI Cinematographer, Agility

No copy of the posting was saved when this application was built on 2026-08-21, and this folder never had a 1-job-reference.md. The notes below were pieced together on 2026-10-14. They are not the posting's own wording.

## Role and Company
- **Role:** AI Cinematographer. Agility's own calendar invites used "AI Cinematographer" (cultural interview, 2026-09-11) and "AI Producer" (technical interview, 2026-08-25). A job-aggregator listing on jobright.ai carries the title "AI Video Producer/Cinematographer."
- **Company:** Agility (agilityads.com), a precision brand advertising company. It runs targeted ads across connected TV (CTV), online video, mobile, display and other channels.
- **Office:** 1557 West Innovation Way, Ste 500, Lehi, UT 84043 (from the hiring manager's email signature).
- **Hiring contact:** Eric Wood, Head of Performance Creative.
- **Pay:** Not recorded anywhere.
- **Work mode:** Not recorded. Every interview so far was held over Google Meet.

## Duties
Taken from a search-engine summary of the jobright.ai listing, not from the posting text:
- Produce AI-generated video ads, applying cinematography fundamentals.
- Turn briefs, scripts and shot lists into finished sequences with generative AI tools.
- Build character reference sheets and style guides to keep visuals consistent.
- Handle post-production through final delivery: editing, color, sound and voiceover.
- Adapt work for CTV, online video (OLV) and social, and meet deadlines within the company's SLA framework.

## Requirements
Same source as the duties:
- 3+ years of professional video or cinematography experience.
- A reel or portfolio.
- Experience with AI creative tools. Claude, Higgsfield and other generative platforms are named.

## Where It Was Listed
- jobright.ai (aggregator): https://jobright.ai/jobs/info/6a5a7529856af468ab0089d7. The page could not be opened from this environment, so the summary above came from search results.

research.overview: Agility (agilityads.com, also listed as Agility Ads or Agility Digital, Inc.) is a small Utah ad-tech company that sells what it calls precision brand advertising. Its platform runs targeted ads across connected TV, mobile, display and the open web. The hiring manager's email signature gives the office as 1557 West Innovation Way, Ste 500, Lehi, UT. Some company profiles list Draper, UT instead. CEO Matt Behrend calls the product 'the first brand advertising operating system'. The company began as a small geofencing agency that he bought about four and a half years before a September 2025 profile. Clinch became its main ad-serving and dynamic-creative partner in June 2024. Headcount is about 51 to 100 (Built In lists 68). Funding figures conflict: one profile says $3.7M in total, another says $15.7M. This is not the same company as Agility the Kuwait logistics firm, Agility Robotics, Agility CMS or Agility Recovery, and most 'Agility' review pages online belong to those companies.

glassdoor.summary: Company-wide reviews, not team-specific. The sample is small, and many reviews come from Lehi employees around March 2025, about 19 months old now. Search snippets show 85% would recommend, 92% CEO approval and a 4.4 compensation and benefits score. People, transparency and leadership that listens to feedback get the most praise. Complaints are about growing pains, slow decisions ('analysis paralysis') and constant change. One former employee wrote that the product 'isn't real. Just the trade desk with lipstick.' One review mentions a DSV buyout, which matches the unrelated logistics company, so a few reviews on this page may be misfiled. Glassdoor could not be opened directly, so these figures come from search results. Do not use the larger 'Agility' page (E39227, 727 reviews), which is the logistics company.

indeed.summary: No Indeed company page tied to agilityads.com came up. The Indeed 'Agility' page (3.6 stars, 109 reviews) belongs to the Kuwait logistics company, not this employer. The Indeed connector failed to connect today, so get_company_data could not be run.

reddit.summary: Two searches, one general and one limited to site:reddit.com, found no Reddit threads about Agility Ads or agilityads.com.

pros.point: Reviewers most often praise the people. They describe a culture of transparency and say leadership genuinely listens to feedback.
Ratings are strong for a small company: 4.5 overall from 33 reviews, 85% would recommend, and compensation and benefits rated 4.4. These are company-wide reviews from a small sample.

Creative is central to the product. The 2024 Clinch partnership was set up to run dynamic, persona-tailored ads across display, mobile, CTV, audio and digital out-of-home. That makes an AI video and cinematography role core work, not a side function.
Leadership is openly betting on generative AI. The CEO says generative AI will speed up the need for the brand-advertising tools Agility sells, which fits a role built around AI-generated ads.

The work is measured. One reviewer points to large brand-advertising budgets to win and calls the tracking 'second to none'. A content marketing reviewer in Lehi says it is a fun place with a real chance to make an impact.
At roughly 51 to 100 people (Built In lists 68), one person's work is visible, and the head of performance creative did his interviews himself.

cons.point: The review base is thin and dated: 33 reviews in total, many from around March 2025. At least one review (mentioning a DSV buyout) looks misfiled from the logistics company of the same name.
Growing pains show up in several reviews: trouble adopting new processes, 'analysis paralysis' on decisions, and constant change that takes comfort with continuous learning.

There is sharp criticism among the negative reviews. One former employee wrote that the product 'isn't real. Just the trade desk with lipstick,' and other negative reviews point to problems with leadership and feedback in a startup-style setting.

Customer-side reviews are mixed: 3.6 stars from 14 reviews on Birdeye. One customer called the communication one of the worst they had seen in the ad space, while another praised the service team. These are customer reviews, not employee reviews.

Little reliable public information exists about the company's finances. Funding is reported as $3.7M by one profile and $15.7M by another, the founding year ranges from 2014 to 2018, and headquarters is listed as both Draper and Lehi.

red_flags: Same-name confusion: most 'Agility' review pages (Glassdoor E39227 with 727 reviews, Indeed 3.6 with 109 reviews) are the Kuwait logistics company. Use only Glassdoor E2942214 for this employer.
No reply from Agility to Joshua's 2026-09-24 follow-up to Eric Wood (cc Kayla), checked in Gmail on 2026-10-14. The last contact from Agility was the 2026-09-11 cultural interview.
Pay and remote policy for this role do not appear in anything saved. The office is in Lehi, Utah, about 630 driving miles from Mesa.
research.bottom_line: Small Utah ad-tech company (about 50 to 100 people) with good but thin and dated Glassdoor reviews: 4.5 from 33, mostly from early 2025. People and transparency get praise. Growing pains and constant change are the usual complaints, plus one sharp critique of the product. The role fits the company's direction, since creative and generative AI are central to what it sells. Three things are still open: pay, whether the job can be done remotely from Mesa, and where the process stands after three rounds and an unanswered follow-up.
